title: Bayesian Networks & d-Separation
interviewAnswer: A Bayesian network is a DAG that factorizes a joint distribution into local conditional distributions; d-separation encodes conditional-independence relationships.
why: Graphical models represent complex joint distributions in a structured, interpretable way.
intuition: Each node only needs a conditional model given its parents rather than one giant joint probability table.
deepDive: p(x1,…,xn)=∏p(xi|parents_i). Graph structure determines independence properties, but a causal interpretation requires additional assumptions beyond probability factorization.
commonMistakes: Assuming every Bayesian network is causal.
production: Use graphs to make assumptions explicit; dense networks can make inference computationally expensive.
workedExample: Rain→WetGrass←Sprinkler is a collider; conditioning on WetGrass can make Rain and Sprinkler dependent.
